x: 2 Miles Walk Handicap—L Storey (460), 1 ; W. G Dodkin (365), 2 ; C.

The race was keenly contested throughout; the long markers making every effort to keep in front; and it was not until the last mile that the faster men appeared likely to overtake those two very youthful walkers, C.
Ken O'Kell, our ex-champion from Stoke, came to revive old acquaintance and turned out in this event. Walking in excellent style, C.

Quite a number of our walkers competed in the 3 mile track race on Boxing Day and C W. Redgrave, who won the previous year's race, was again the winner, but this time in a tight finish with A A Harley.
I only hope that Micky Pyer and Harry Bruce will follow Jack's example. C.
At the City Police Meeting C.

Arthur Allum once again showed that Christmas festivities do not affect him and his was a very fine performance considering the large field which competed. A good field started in the Walk and it was soon seen that a close race would ensue between those two young walkers of infinite promise, C.
Thorn kept Len company for a while, but then experienced leg trouble which caused him to stop for a few minutes and lose several places which could not afterwards be regained. Meanwhile, C.
Elson made a bold bid for it and in the early stages of the race he got away from C.
Elson also came under the judges' ban and with C.
Harley, who was out to fight his utmost all the way, and who, in turn, had gained a slight lead from C.
Webb, beat the second Cadogan walker, C.
Len Fletcher suffered (we use the word advisedly) disqualification, and Harold King led our team in, finishing fourth. C.
Final: Michael, 1; Tame, 2; Carter, 3; Brown, 4; Ford, 5; Scrimshaw, 6. 2 Miles Walk.—C.

Thorn, a former winner, and C.
